Information since May points to continued labor-market strength and solid economic activity, with inflation near the 2 percent objective. In New Keynesian/Taylor-rule frameworks (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), such conditions justify measured rate hikes; the “symmetric 2 percent” language aligns with inflation-targeting best practice and anchoring of expectations (Svensson and Woodford, 2005), which the statement notes are little changed. The implementation details—IOER set 5 bps below the top of the target range and use of ON RRP—reflect modern floor-system operating principles for precise short-rate control (Goodfriend, 2002). Strong business investment and firmer household spending are positive signals, while the move toward gradual normalization introduces a mild hawkish tilt but keeps risks “roughly balanced,” which helps limit financial-friction spillovers consistent with financial accelerator insights. Overall tone: moderately positive with cautious normalization.
